response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ma.department AS department, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM income i JOIN member m ON i.link_to_member = m.member_id JOIN major ma ON m.link_to_major = ma.major_id GROUP BY ma.department), s AS (SELECT department, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_share_minus_avg FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Departments are grouped by the major.department text value, so different majors sharing a department name are combined into one department.
The average of shares is taken across all departments with at least one qualifying income record (departments with zero records do not appear).
